newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bankers see punctual EMU start.
newsitem.headline: German bankers see punctual EMU start.

text.p: The German Banking Fedreation (BdB) said on Monday that it expected European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) to start punctually.

"Despite the sceptical voices which are being raised again at present, the banks are expecting EMU to start punctually on January 1, 1999," BdB president Karl-Heinz Wessel said in the text of a speech to be delivered at a news conference.
However, Wessel said Germany still had a lot to do to prepare itself for EMU.
Wessel said it was crucial that Germany's outstanding mark-denominated government date should be converted into Euros from EMU start.
Wessel also called for the abolition of minimum reserves, arguing that they were not essential for monetary policy.
German banks have been complaining for years to have minimum reserves abolished, arguing that they put them at a competitive disadvantage.
German banks are currently obliged to hold non-interest-bearing deposits with the Bundesbank, a rule that does not apply in some other EU states.
